Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider the concept of one-hot encoding. When you one-hot encode a categorical variable with \( $$n$$ \) categories, you create \( $$n$$ \) binary columns, each representing one category. However, if you include all \( $$n$$ \) columns, they will be linearly dependent because the sum of these columns will always equal $$1$$ for each observation.

**Hint 2:** Think about the rank of a matrix. A matrix is full column rank if its columns are linearly independent. When you one-hot encode a categorical variable and include all categories, the columns are not linearly independent. This is because one column can be expressed as a linear combination of the others.
